subject: Hosted API pricing — Skybridge usage recap & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Romero <alex@skybridge.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05T15:03:00Z
Subject: Quick recap from today's discovery — monthly volume & burst profile

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful walkthrough of Redwood's hosted API and the Dedicated options. Per our internal sync I wanted to put the usage shape we discussed in writing so we can get a ballpark on pricing and any recommended configuration.

Summary of expected traffic (rough):
- Typical monthly tokens: ~2.4B tokens/month (chat prompts + responses).
- Baseline daily steady-state: ~80M tokens/day.
- Anticipated burst window: 90–120s windows during marketing push, peak concurrency estimate ~1,000–1,300 TPS for ~10–20 minutes; 99th pct sustained ~400 TPS for ~1 hour.
- Embeddings usage is small initially (~15M embeddings units/month).

Budget guidance: we are targeting a cost of roughly $500–800 per 1M tokens for hosted API in this POC/early customer phase, but we are flexible if there are clear unit-econ tradeoffs (e.g., quantized models, reserved capacity).

Please send a short recap with any assumptions you used for unit pricing, whether our peak TPS would require a Dedicated setup vs. hosted (and estimated lead time), and any recommended mitigations (batching, prefix caching, model variants). Attached a tiny traffic sample and a one-sheet with endpoints.

Next steps from us: procurement will want an initial SOW and a mid-Nov implementation window if costs align.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Romero
Head of Product
Skybridge AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex@skybridge.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-06T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today's discovery — monthly volume & burst profile

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and sample. This is exactly what we need to size options and give a practical cost range. I took a pass with a few initial assumptions (below) and attached a simple mapping file that shows how token slabs + burst support map to dollar ranges.

Assumptions I used for the attached map (see 20261005-skybridge-map.xlsx):
- Baseline model: r-instruct-1.3 (production, non-quantized) for chat generation; fallback to r-instruct-1.3-8bit for cost-sensitive endpoints.
- Steady-state batching/aggregation: average request grouping reduces per-token infra cost by ~8–12% in our model.
- Burst handling: hosted autoscale can cover short 10–20 minute windows up to ~500–600 TPS without transition; >600 TPS sustained for minutes likely needs Dedicated or multi-region routing.
- SLA target: 99th pct latency SLO for user-facing endpoints; we can provide a canary plan for the marketing push.

Ballpark hosted API ranges (monthly, $ per 1M tokens) based on the slabs you gave: 
- POC / pay-as-you-go (no reservation): $720–$920 per 1M tokens depending on mix of quantized vs full fp16 model.
- Committed reserved (3–6 month commit): $480–$650 per 1M with burst credit & soft-reserve.
- Dedicated estimate (reserved capacity + throughput SLAs): contact us for line-item estimate — roughly similar unit economics to committed reserved once amortized across capacity, but with stronger peak guarantees.

For your stated peak (1,000–1,300 TPS):
- Short marketing bursts (<=20m) — we recommend routed hosted with multi-region fallback and pre-warmed concurrency; we can support up to ~900–1,000 TPS without a Dedicated commitment, depending on model variant.
- If you need a hard guarantee for 1,300 TPS, we should size Dedicated pools; that's where burst guarantees and predictable throughput matter.

Requested next steps:
1) Can you confirm the % of requests expected to hit the large-generation vs short snippets? (This affects average token/req and billing mix.)
2) Procurement contact + target SOW budget range (we can provide a draft SOW once procurement confirms a target band).
3) If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min ops call to walk the traffic sample and model suggestions — Karthik and Jordan are available next Tue/Wed.

I'll loop in pricing with a follow-up that includes a simple three-tier price table and an ops checklist for the burst.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: 20261005-skybridge-map.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-07T13:44:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — quick operational notes and cost lever options

Alex / team — quick operational notes from our infra side to supplement Marissa's pricing summary.

Operational notes and cost levers to consider:
- Model choice: shifting 30% of high-volume endpoints to our 8-bit variant typically drops unit cost ~30% with minimal observable quality delta for short prompts.
- KV prefix caching: if you have repeated system prompts or shared few-shot contexts, enabling prefix caching can cut generation tokens by 10–25% in practice.
- Intelligent routing: we can route low-latency needs to a smaller fp16 pool and batchable/background jobs to a quantized pool to optimize both latency and cost.
- Burst protection: for predictable marketing pushes we recommend a short pre-warm (1–2 hours) and a light Dedicated buffer to guarantee headroom. That buffer can be smaller than full Dedicated pool and saves cost.

Estimated concrete pricing for the numbers Alex provided (month 1 POC mix: 60% gen / 40% short completions):
- PAYG hosted: ~$860 per 1M tokens (reflects mix, no commit).
- 3-month commit: ~$540 per 1M tokens (with burst credit and a small reserved buffer).
- Dedicated + buffer: effective ~$520 per 1M tokens after amortization of fixed capacity but requires a minimum monthly commitment (~$XXk — we'll surface exacts in the SOW).

We can prepare a one-page pricing appendix that maps monthly token slabs to concrete line-items (model, network, burst buffer). Marissa — I'll draft that and include a recommended SLO and ops-runbook for the push.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
